That wouldn't be terrible... I'm not big on running an OS from a USB since someone could literally walk away with your entire "system," and most OS's will configure themselves for your hardware... meaning you may run into issues when you switch from one computer to another.

I just keep the bootable live-CD of Arch on a USB, that way I avoid both of these issues. It's not persistent, so nobody's taking my data, and it's configured to boot on almost all systems, so you won't run into issues where the OS is installed for processor A and refuses to work on a different computer with processor B.

There is a bootable iso called boot-repair-disk (formerly boot-repair-cd) which can help you fix it.

I used it a lot on an installation with a small boot partition and automatic updates.

Before anything else, I strongly recommend booting a live media and backing up your valuable files to external media first. Having done so, this may help you:
